\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{طريق} (ṭarīq)}{طريق (ṭarīq)}]{\ar{طريق} (ṭarīq) — a road}

\label{lesson:AR-C91-tariq}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a shop, then the Arabic for a street.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{طريق}}
\textbf{\ar{طريق}} — \emph{ṭarīq} — \textquotedblleft{}a road\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{طريق}} (\emph{ṭarīq}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ṭ-r-q}, \textquotedblleft{}to strike, to beat\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Lane's \emph{ṭarīq} is a beaten track, a road.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭarīq}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭarīq}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{ṭarīq}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a shop, then the Arabic for a street, then say \emph{ṭarīq} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{طريق} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A road\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{بنك} (bank)}{بنك (bank)}]{\ar{بنك} (bank) — a bank}

\label{lesson:AR-C91-bank}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a street, then the Arabic for a road.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{بنك}}
\textbf{\ar{بنك}} — \emph{bank} — \textquotedblleft{}a bank\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{بنك}} (\emph{bank}) is borrowed from the European word, Italian \emph{banco} or French \emph{banque}, \textquotedblleft{}bank\textquotedblright{}, once a moneychanger's bench; it has no Arabic root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bank}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{bank}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a street, then the Arabic for a road, then say \emph{bank} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{بنك} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A bank\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{محطة} (maḥaṭṭa)}{محطة (maḥaṭṭa)}]{\ar{محطة} (maḥaṭṭa) — a station}

\label{lesson:AR-C91-mahatta}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a road, then the Arabic for a bank.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{محطة}}
\textbf{\ar{محطة}} — \emph{maḥaṭṭa} — \textquotedblleft{}a station\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{محطة}} (\emph{maḥaṭṭa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḥ-ṭ-ṭ}, \textquotedblleft{}to put down, to set down\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Maḥaṭṭa} is the \emph{ma-} place noun, \textquotedblleft{}a place of setting down, a halt\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a road, then the Arabic for a bank, then say \emph{maḥaṭṭa} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{سيارة} (sayyāra)}{سيارة (sayyāra)}]{\ar{سيارة} (sayyāra) — a car}

\label{lesson:AR-C91-sayyara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a bank, then the Arabic for a station.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{سيارة}}
\textbf{\ar{سيارة}} — \emph{sayyāra} — \textquotedblleft{}a car\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{سيارة}} (\emph{sayyāra}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{s-y-r}, \textquotedblleft{}to go, to travel\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Lane gives \emph{sayyāra} as a company of travellers, a caravan; the car is a modern sense.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{حافلة} (ḥāfila)}{حافلة (ḥāfila)}]{\ar{حافلة} (ḥāfila) — a bus}

\label{lesson:AR-C91-hafila}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a station, then the Arabic for a car.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{حافلة}}
\textbf{\ar{حافلة}} — \emph{ḥāfila} — \textquotedblleft{}a bus\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{حافلة}} (\emph{ḥāfila}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḥ-f-l}, \textquotedblleft{}to gather, to fill\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Lane's \emph{ḥāfil} is a full udder or a valley in flood; as the word for a bus \emph{ḥāfila} is a modern coinage.
\end{cousinweb}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a station, then the Arabic for a car, then say \emph{ḥāfila} again
\end{itemize}
